assumptions: Reasoning and thinking tokens are billed as output; the run record counts them inside outputTokens.
OpenAI's long-context prices start above 272K input tokens per request; no call of these cases comes near it, so they are not in the table.

claude-haiku-5-5 is priced per request by prompt length: a request over 100,000 prompt tokens pays the prices under `over`. A run record holds a phase's total, not each call, so the tier is applied when a phase's input tokens divided by its calls pass the threshold.

cachedInput for the Claude models is the cache-hit price. Chartula 0.1.0-preview.5 sets no cache breakpoint on Anthropic requests, so no cache write (1.25x input) is expected; a record that reports cached input there needs a second look.
claude-haiku-5-5 counts the same text as about 30% more tokens than the earlier Claude tokenizer, so its token counts do not compare one to one with the other models'.
